thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: high-sev - Customer AcmeCorp reporting intermittent failures resolving their VPC endpoint (private edge) in us-west-3a. Observed 502/timeout from app -> private endpoint. Triggered by synthetic checks. Paging on-call.

alice_sre: Acknowledged. I'm on call. pinging netops and customer success. Can someone collect customer traceroutes/DNS results while I look at SRE metrics?

ben_netops: Looking. I see a spike in DNS NXDOMAINs from probes located in us-west-3a and 3b starting ~2080112000. Route table looks normal. No recent route changes in our infra. Investigating TGW and VPC endpoint state.

carmen_eng: From app logs: lots of connect timeouts to 10.95.34.12:443 (customer endpoint). App uses internal resolver 169.254.169.253? will grab dig from pod when alice says.

dan_cust_success: AcmeCorp confirmed they're seeing failures from their on-prem->DC to the endpoint too. They've opened a ticket with carrier as well. They're seeing intermittent NXDOMAIN, then eventually correct A -> private IP.

alice_sre: Running quick dig from test host in us-west-3a:
```
$ dig +short acme-endpoint.vpce.internal
;; -> sometimes empty
$ dig acme-endpoint.vpce.internal @10.2.3.5
;; -> NXDOMAIN
$ dig acme-endpoint.vpce.internal @10.2.3.6
;; -> 10.95.34.12
```
Looks like resolver inconsistency between our local resolvers (10.2.3.5 vs 10.2.3.6)

ben_netops: Pulling DNS server logs. 10.2.3.5 shows an error: "zone transfer mismatch" and refuses to answer for the privatelink zone. 10.2.3.6 is healthy. Both in same AZ but different hosts. Spinning up more logs.

alice_sre: Any recent config changes pushed to the DNS fleet? Querying eng-infra.

carmen_eng: No infra DNS changes in last 24h from our config repo. There's a rolling cert rotation that touched the dns auth agent yesterday but it was marked successful.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident severity auto-upgraded to SEV2 due to customer impact (support ticket + synthetic failures). Paging platform lead.

ben_netops: I can repro with tcpdump on 10.2.3.5: seeing truncated responses and malformed SOA in some replies. Suspect a partial config corruption on that resolver instance. I'm going to drain traffic from 10.2.3.5 (iptables redirect) and failover to healthy instance 10.2.3.7. ETA 60s.

alice_sre: Go ahead. Make sure to annotate runbook. If failover works, we'll keep traffic on 10.2.3.7 and plan a restart/replace for 10.2.3.5.

ben_netops: Executed:
```
sudo iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p udp --dport 53 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.2.3.7:53
sudo iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 53 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.2.3.7:53
```
Traffic now going to 10.2.3.7

alice_sre: Observability -> synthetic checks now show success. Customer reported restored resolution. Monitoring for 10m.

dan_cust_success: AcmeCorp confirms services back to normal. Thanks team. They asked for RCA and time window. I'll keep them updated.

carmen_eng: Good candidate RCA: single DNS resolver instance had corrupted zone data (SOA/AXFR mismatch). Follow-up: replace instance, audit cert rotation agent, and add resolver-level healthcheck and zone-consistency alerts.

cloud-provider-bot: Provider ticket created: #CP-998172 - Investigating networking flaps reported in us-west-3a affecting shared resolver path. Assigned to provider-NOC.

alice_sre: Next steps (short):
- ben to terminate/replace 10.2.3.5 (done as maintenance) and validate replication.
- carmen to add zone-consistency check to DNS healthchecks.
- dan to send interim customer update with timeframe and mitigations.

ben_netops: Replaced instance 10.2.3.5 -> new 10.2.3.9 bootstrapped, AXFR validated, removed iptables DNAT rules. All resolvers show consistent zone serials.

alice_sre: Closing paging loop. Will create postmortem template and assign owners. If anyone needs follow-up, flag here. :white_check_mark:

dan_cust_success: Sending customer note now. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: SEV2 -> mitigated at 2080112600. Root cause under investigation; follow-up postmortem required.
